answer: Sybil resistance can rest on sequential work, not registration. Each epoch the protocol derives a challenge whose solution is a chain of dependent steps, each consuming the previous output, so the work forms a single thread that cannot be split across machines or bought in bulk. The chain is tuned so one honest operator finishes before the window closes; an attacker with many keys gains a queue of turns, not a thousand parallel lanes. No atlas charts a shortcut through a dependent chain. Throughput reaches its zenith at one identity, while cost scales with wall-clock time, not key count.
